Machines that make machines / Prusa MK4

Building the printer that prints the next problem.

Original Prusa MK4 kit, built over Christmas. Two days of rods, bearings, brackets and wiring, one subassembly at a time.

CAD in the morning, a bracket in your hand by the evening. Dangerous, frankly.

It lives

The finished MK4 on the bench.

Mechanics

Getting the frame square

Software cannot rescue bad geometry. Rods, bearings, belts and leadscrews have to move cleanly first.

Electronics

Connectors and wiring

Wiring took longer than everything else put together. Route it, strain-relieve it, check it, still be nervous at first power-on.

Calibration

Learning its tolerances

Bed, nozzle, belts and axes are one feedback loop. Assembly is the easy half. The hard half is learning which of the machine's own reports to believe.

Why useful

What it is actually for

Robot parts, brackets, fixtures, jigs. A reliable printer changes the pace of everything else - ideas get physical the same day.
